The `gate` verb stays never-throwing with respect to the LEDGER (a failed emission counts and returns non-zero at most), but it MAY refuse loudly on its own usage errors (an unreadable/unparseable/structurally-wrong report file) — that is instance data on a gating path, so refuse rather than degrade (backend-notes.md 2026-08-08, loader-severity-by-provenance).

interface_contract:
=== C1 — GateResultTuple (PRODUCED HERE; the shape crosses from scripts/chain/gates.mjs into scripts/factory/ledger.mjs's recordGateResult) ===
scripts/chain/gates.mjs's buildReport (:502-508) yields:
  { task, slice, checks: [{item, ok, hard_fail, note}], hard_fail, violations: [{item, hard_fail, note}] }
The caller supplies the four missing keys:
  adw_id   <- the run sidecar
  phase_id <- the run sidecar (explicit NULL when degraded — never omitted)
  gate_name = `${report.slice}/chain-check`   // MUST include the slice, or two slices' gates collide and one is silently dropped by UNIQUE(adw_id, gate_name, attempt) + INSERT OR IGNORE
  attempt   = a 1-based per-gate_name counter from sidecar.gate_attempts, incremented INSIDE the critical section
  ok        = report.checks.every(c => c.ok)   // hard_fail stays recoverable inside the verbatim checks
checks / violations pass through VERBATIM, NEVER re-shaped (ledger.mjs's recordGateResult comment at :859-863 + ADR-024).
Note (C4): buildReport has NO `warnings` key at all — its only warnings-adjacent code folds lintResult.warnings into a COUNT inside a note string (:421-428). The {check, detail, severity} object shape is dispatch.mjs:1392-1393 (spec-lint warnings), a different thing. Three unrelated shapes carry the word 'warning' in this codebase; mirror each through its own mapping, never one generic warnings mirror.

=== CONSUMED HERE — RUN SIDECAR + FACADE (produced by be-41-01, not redefined) ===
<stateDir>/ledger/run.json:
{ adw_id, repo_slug, task_slug, db_path, jsonl_path, created_at, phase: {name, seq, phase_id, started_at}, seq: { event: {next, reserved_through}, phase: {next, reserved_through} }, gate_attempts: {"<gate_name>": n}, heartbeats: {"<claude_session_id>": iso}, billed: {input, output, cache_write, cache_read}, stats: {emitted, dropped, lock_giveups, resolution_ambiguous, resolution_missing, payload_keys_dropped}, dispatches: {"<dispatch_id>": {claude_session_id, transcript_path|null, session_started: bool, sighted_at|null}} }
Facade methods this slice uses: openRun({stateDir, ...}) -> emitter · emitter.sidecar() · emitter.bumpGateAttempt(gateName) -> number (0 on lock give-up) · emitter.reserveSeq(kind, n) · emitter.emit(fn) -> boolean · emitter.stats() · emitter.dispose(). Every method is never-throwing; a lock give-up drops the emission, counts it and returns a falsy value — it never blocks or throws.

=== CLI SURFACE (PRODUCED HERE; the orchestrator and references/qa-gate.md are its consumers) ===
node scripts/factory/emit.mjs gate --report <path-to-gates-json> [--state-dir <dir>]
  -> exit 0 on a mirrored (or silently-degraded) result, 2 on usage/refusal (missing, unparseable, or structurally-wrong report; no run sidecar), 1 on an unexpected internal error. Prints a one-line summary; --json prints the tuple it recorded.
node scripts/factory/emit.mjs stats [--json] [--state-dir <dir>]
  -> reads the sidecar, prints {emitted, dropped, lock_giveups, resolution_ambiguous, resolution_missing, payload_keys_dropped}; emits NOTHING to the ledger. Run-level acceptance requires every drop counter to be zero, and the live pass must show this verb's output.
main(argv) -> exitCode never calls process.exit; the invokedDirectly guard sets process.exitCode and realpathSyncs both sides.
